scatter-radar-space-research-from-the-gr.title: Scatter radar: Space research from the ground
scatter-radar-space-research-from-the-gr.creator: National Archives and Records Administration
scatter-radar-space-research-from-the-gr.synopsis: This 1963 National Bureau of Standards film documents the development of Peru’s Jicamarca Observatory, from the search for a site near the magnetic equator through construction of its 22-acre antenna and powerful radar system. It explains how incoherent-scatter radar measures electrons in the upper atmosphere and highlights cooperation between U.S. researchers, Peru’s Instituto Geofísico del Perú, and local workers and technicians.

ia.creator: National Archives and Records Administration
ia.subject: archives.gov;public.resource.org
ia.description: National Archives and Records Administration - ARC Identifier 37826 / Local Identifier 167.85 - Scatter radar: Space research from the ground - Department of Commerce. National Bureau of Standards. (1934 - 08/23/1988). Tells the story of Jicamarca Observatory, new National Bureau of Standards facility near Lima, Peru, and its fascinating new reserach projects. Jicamarca, largest institution of its kind in the world, uses a 22 acre antenna, probes the upper atmosphere to measure electron densities, makes observations of planets, and studies solar coronas and solar gases. Presents in a travelogue-like sequence, the search for a site for the Observatory near the magnetic equator, watches construction go forward in the arid Jicamarca Valley at the foot of the Andes, and, throughout, observes the cooperation of the Peruvian people and of the Instituto Geofisico del Peru, famous and historic ally-in-science of the National Bureau of Standards. The scatter radar technique is explained in simple animation sequences: high frequency radio waves penetrate the ionosphere; free electrons in the upper atmosphere respond by oscillating and scattering their energy incoherently; the ultra-powerful Jicamarca antenna picks up this faint incoherent scatter. Analysis of this new data, yielding information heretofore concealed, provides the basis for calling this new technique "space research from the ground." DVD copied by IASL Master Scanner Timothy Vollmer.

Emphasizes the need for immediate reseeding to prevent floods. Made possible by a donation from John and Paige Curran.

troubleshooting-electric-circuits.title: TROUBLESHOOTING ELECTRIC CIRCUITS
troubleshooting-electric-circuits.creator: Department of Defense
troubleshooting-electric-circuits.synopsis: The film teaches electricians how to diagnose and repair wiring faults while reducing fire, electrical, and equipment hazards at Air Force installations. A basic lighting circuit introduces the power source, conductors, switch, load, and protective fuse or circuit breaker. The film distinguishes three common faults: a short circuit connects hot and neutral conductors, a grounded circuit connects the hot conductor to grounded metal, and an open circuit breaks continuity and stops current flow.\n\nPractical examples use an ohmmeter, a buzzer-type continuity tester, and a voltage tester to identify each fault and narrow its location one section at a time. Electricians are instructed to disconnect power before continuity testing, isolate circuit components, repair the defective wire or connection, retest the circuit, and only then restore power. The closing procedure calls for an operational check, visual inspection, review of any available schematic, analysis of the findings, location of the fault, and repair.

modesta.synopsis: Framed as an old tale from an unnamed island, the film follows Modesta, a pregnant homemaker who cares for a young child and manages the household while her husband orders coffee and a cooked chicken. When the chicken escapes, her husband ridicules her pregnancy, dismisses women’s work, and threatens her, while other women describe the same exhausting labor and lack of consideration.\n\nModesta and her neighbors form the LML, the League of Liberated Women, choose a piece of firewood as their symbol, and demand freedom from beatings, shared responsibility for children and housework, and fair treatment in marriage. They confront the men and refuse to cook until the men respond; the men eventually acknowledge women’s right to fair treatment and reject violence, but they refuse to wash diapers and add conditions of their own. The closing lines claim that civilization has ended such conflicts, then undercut that claim by asking whether women have truly stopped using pieces of firewood.

Biblical quotations and comparisons with homes, museums, and shelter from a storm explain that entry is free to believers because Christ paid the price with his blood. Simple sets and labeled props show a man confronting doors and carrying burdens such as unbelief, money, and anxiety.\n\nAnyone seeking heaven must leave behind sin, unbelief, riches, fame, suffering, sorrow, disappointment, and worry, while encouraging other people to accept Jesus. The film repeatedly urges viewers to accept Jesus as their savior without delay, warning that God will someday close the door. An open doorway against a field of stars accompanies the final invitation, followed by a hymn about the saints and their heavenly home.

ia.creator: Baptista (C.O.) Films

this-is-coffee.title: This is Coffee

this-is-coffee.synopsis: Coffee beans, plantation workers, grinding equipment, and brewed cups introduce coffee as a product of tropical cultivation, processing, and human labor. A stylized tribute to factory workers and mass production, it was selected for the National Film Registry in 1999.

ia.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
ia.subject: Automobiles: Manufacturing;Labor: 1930s;Occupations: Automotive
ia.description: Classic "capitalist realist" drama showing the manufacture of Chevrolets from foundry to finished vehicles. Though ostensibly a tribute to the "master hands" of the assembly line workers, it seems more of a paean to the designers of this impressive mass production system. Filmed in Flint, Michigan, just months before the United Auto Workers won union recognition with their famous sitdown strikes. Released the same year as two other films with which it shares similarities: MODERN TIMES and TRIUMPH OF THE WILL. Selected for the 1999 National Film Registry of "artistically, culturally, and socially significant" films.

your-movie-camera-and-how-to-use-it-456b.title: Your Movie Camera and How to Use It
your-movie-camera-and-how-to-use-it-456b.synopsis: *Your Movie Camera and How to Use It* is an instructional film on making better home movies. It explains correct film exposure through the camera’s diaphragm, relating its operation to the human eye, and recommends adjusting the aperture for changing light. It also demonstrates angled composition, perspective, depth, and reviewing footage while urging viewers to study the instruction manual.

expedition-29-crew-profile-6-crew-member.title: Expedition 29 Crew Profile - 6 Crew Members

NASA astronauts Mike Fossum and Dan Burbank; JAXA astronaut Satoshi Furukawa; and Russian cosmonauts Anton Shkaplerov, Anatoly Ivanishin and Sergey Volkov discuss their mission and the benefits of space travel. Product Title: Expedition 29 Crew Profile Version 2 Reference Master Number: 884586 JSC Production Number: JSC 2523 Length: 11:56

where-the-sun-reigns-0b0df04b.synopsis: Where the Sun Reigns presents a scenic tour of Miami-Dade County, from Greater Miami and Miami Beach to the Florida Keys. Ground-level and helicopter views showcase ocean beaches, swimming, jai alai, golf courses, Villa Vizcaya’s art collections, modern auditoriums, and convention facilities, portraying South Florida as a destination for recreation, culture, and visitors.

ia.creator: Reela Films

ia.description: Tour of the scenic Miami-Dade County area. With many views of attractions at ground level and from a helicopter. Director: John Behney.

climate-factor-a7c554f5.title: Climate Factor
climate-factor-a7c554f5.creator: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
climate-factor-a7c554f5.synopsis: This 1984 NOAA film examines how climate shapes shelter, clothing, food, and human migration. It also traces Earth’s geological and climatic changes over the past 100 million years and considers climate’s possible role in the dinosaurs’ disappearance.

ia.creator: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
ia.subject: FedFlix; ntis.gov
ia.description: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration The Climate Factor AVA11754VNB1 - 1984 Analyzes the ways in which climate affects our daily lives, from the forms of shelter and clothing we need to the types of food we eat. Shows how climatic changes in the past have caused whole populations to move and may even be responsible for the disappearance of the dinosaur. Traces geologic changes that the earth has undergone in the past 100 million years.

fashion-s-favorite-part-ii-e215b888.title: Fashion's Favorite (Part II)
fashion-s-favorite-part-ii-e215b888.synopsis: Beginning with an hourglass and a montage of household appliances, this industrial film presents DuPont’s claim that its products make life more livable before tracing rayon manufacture. Cellulose is steeped in sodium hydroxide, converted into xanthate, dissolved into spinning solution, and extruded through spinnerets into dry filaments. Microscopic inspection and fabric applications complete the presentation.

ia.description: Opens with a shot of an hourglass which leads into a montage of various household appliances and then moves into a discussion of how DuPont "makes life more liveable." The rest of the film tracks the manufacturing of rayon from raw material to finished product.

home-electrical-appliances-02267047.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films
home-electrical-appliances-02267047.synopsis: This 1944 educational film explains the electrical and physical principles behind household appliances, including irons, incandescent and fluorescent lamps, vacuum cleaners, and refrigerators. Through demonstrations and animation, it covers household circuits, resistance heating, thermostats, electric motors, refrigeration, and basic appliance maintenance and repair.

ia.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films
ia.subject: Electricity;Houses and homes: Appliances;Appliances

inside-outside-the-story-of-food-and-fit.title: Inside/Outside: The Story of Food and Fitness
inside-outside-the-story-of-food-and-fit.creator: Department of Agriculture
inside-outside-the-story-of-food-and-fit.synopsis: *Inside/Outside: The Story of Food and Fitness* presents the body as calling attention to neglected health habits. The film discusses reducing fats, oils, and added sweeteners while choosing fruits, vegetables, and lower-fat milk products for essential vitamins, minerals, starch, and fiber. It concludes by emphasizing regular physical activity, weight awareness, and physician guidance.

modern-trends-in-swine-production-50beab.title: Modern Trends in Swine Production
modern-trends-in-swine-production-50beab.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
modern-trends-in-swine-production-50beab.synopsis: This 1961 agricultural film presents modern approaches to swine production, covering breeding, feeding, farrowing, sanitation, and day-to-day management. It follows preparation of sows for farrowing, clean handling and disinfection of facilities, then moves through nursing, weaning, early piglet care, manure removal, and growth toward market weight. Production schedules, housing space, and feeder allocation support efficient use of labor and equipment.

ia.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
ia.subject: Agriculture: Pigs
ia.description: Up-to-date methods of hog raising, plus suggestions on breeding, feeding, farrowing and management.

duck-and-cover.title: Duck and Cover
duck-and-cover.creator: Archer Productions, Inc.
duck-and-cover.synopsis: This 1951 civil defense film teaches children how to respond to an atomic-bomb warning or a sudden flash. An animated character, Bert the Turtle, withdraws into his shell when danger appears, while children demonstrate how to duck, cover their faces and necks, and shelter under desks or tables. The film explains that an atomic explosion can produce intense light and heat, break windows, damage buildings, and throw people against nearby objects.\n\nScenes in schools, homes, streets, buses, and outdoor areas show children seeking cover quickly and staying down until the danger has passed. Viewers are told to enter a designated safe place after a warning, obey civil defense workers, avoid windows, and use walls, doorways, clothing, or even newspaper for protection when better cover is unavailable. The closing asks children to discuss emergency responses with their teachers and repeatedly answer the question of what to do after seeing a flash: “Duck and cover.”

miracle-of-the-can-part-ii-c1ab27ff.title: Miracle of the Can (Part II)
miracle-of-the-can-part-ii-c1ab27ff.creator: Caravel Films, Inc.
miracle-of-the-can-part-ii-c1ab27ff.synopsis: *Miracle of the Can (Part II)* examines America’s canning and food industries, linking farm harvests to large-scale production, scheduling, transport, and packaging. It shows how cans are formed, sealed, and supplied for seasonal crops, while manufacturers pursue locally available alternatives to tin and develop packaging innovations that preserve freshness and extend can-makers’ expertise beyond metal containers.

ia.creator: Caravel Films, Inc.
ia.subject: Agriculture: Food industry;Agriculture: Farms and farming;Agriculture: Food industry: Canning
ia.description: Panoramic exploration of cans and canning in the United States, with excellent imagery of mass production and agribusiness.

oklahoma-oasis-7aa5d6a0.title: Oklahoma Oasis
oklahoma-oasis-7aa5d6a0.creator: National Park Service
oklahoma-oasis-7aa5d6a0.synopsis: “Oklahoma Oasis” portrays southern Oklahoma’s mineral-rich sulfur, bromide, and freshwater springs, whose waters attracted animals and settlers. It traces the area’s colorful history, including the relocation of Native peoples to Indian Territory and the growth of a springs town. Following Platt National Park’s establishment, the town was moved beyond park boundaries as the protected area expanded.

ia.creator: National Park Service
ia.subject: nps.gov;public.resource.org
ia.description: National Park Service Oklahoma Oasis AVA02633VNB1, 1974 In a dramatic portrayal, Chief Dan George comments on the natural beauty and the colorful history connected with the establishment and development of Platt National Park.

agriculture-new-farms-from-grand-coulee-.synopsis: A newsreel on new farms associated with Grand Coulee, highlighting water infrastructure, electricity, and sustainability.

biological-control-a-natural-alternative.title: Biological Control - A Natural Alternative
biological-control-a-natural-alternative.creator: Department of Agriculture
biological-control-a-natural-alternative.synopsis: This 1989 Department of Agriculture film explains biological control as a natural approach to pest management. It defines biocontrol, outlines its history, and presents practical strategies—including augmentation, recolonization, and inundation—along with examples of successful applications.

under-the-tread-1d8e5b27.title: Under The Tread
under-the-tread-1d8e5b27.synopsis: Under The Tread presents the detailed manufacture of automobile tires, from rubber-coated cord sheets and carefully assembled layers to molding and vulcanization. speaking-of-rubber-part-ii-73947446.title: Speaking of Rubber (Part II)

speaking-of-rubber-part-ii-73947446.synopsis: Narrated by a retired rubber worker, this industrial film surveys rubber’s many uses and the processes behind them. we-drivers-1935-edition-67590a7e.synopsis: *We Drivers* is a driving-safety film examining how physical forces, road conditions, vehicle mechanics, visibility, and driver judgment affect traffic safety. quality-control-in-modern-merchandising-.synopsis: This sponsored film presents modern merchandising as a coordinated process of understanding consumer needs, developing textile specifications, and verifying performance. along-the-way-55c3ecf9.creator: Levene (Carol)

ia.description: "You and Your Bicycle" is a 1948 short film that offers practical guidance on bicycle safety and maintenance, emphasizing the importance of proper riding conduct in urban settings. Set against the backdrop of Oakland, California, the film uses simulated accident scenes alongside authentic street and city footage to illustrate both safe and unsafe biking practices. It covers essential topics such as recognizing hazards on a typical trip to the store, using arm signals, safely carrying bundles, and knowing where to park and ride. The film also warns against dangerous behaviors like stunting, improper passing, hitching rides, and riding double, making it an informative resource aimed at promoting responsible and secure bicycle use.

always-on-call.synopsis: In a dramatized story, Officer Henry responds to concerned neighbors and visits an ill widow who has recently returned from the hospital. She refuses an ambulance and says she will not accept charity, but Henry explains that the Community Chest can arrange a visiting nurse and that patients pay what they can afford. He reassures her that community support comes from people who care about their neighbors.\n\nHenry describes Greater St. Louis Community Chest agencies that help blind and disabled people find work, provide day care and youth programs, rehabilitate injured adults, welcome servicemen, place infants in foster homes, and care for older people. Scenes show children playing and learning, servicemen entering a USO center, a baby receiving care, older adults at a residence, and a nurse visiting a home. The widow recognizes that the same services she once supported can now help her, and the closing appeal asks viewers to contribute one day’s pay to the Community Chest.

frontiers-of-the-future-a-screen-editori.synopsis: In this 1937 film, Lowell Thomas asks where Americans can find opportunity after the nation’s geographic frontiers have closed, then identifies industrial research and invention as the new frontiers. Scenes of oil fields, laboratories, farms, factories, and manufactured goods accompany accounts of how petroleum, chemicals, cotton, coal, and other materials can become useful products. The film connects each successful product with the creation of industries, jobs, and payrolls.\n\nMuch of the discussion centers on chemistry and its possible effects on transportation, agriculture, clothing, food, housing, and health. Thomas lists plastics, synthetic fibers, television, unbreakable lenses, soil-free farming, and other new or experimental products, mixing existing developments with speculative forecasts. He closes by calling industrial scientists and engineers modern pioneers and urging viewers to look toward continued technological progress rather than accept pessimism about America’s future.

day-of-thanksgiving-a.synopsis: Bill Johnson recalls how his family faced Thanksgiving without a turkey after a month of heavy expenses. When the disappointed children say the holiday will be meaningless, their parents ask them to consider what they have beyond a traditional feast, and the family gathers around the dinner table to give thanks.\n\nEach family member names valued parts of daily life, including adequate food and clothing, education, religious choice, family security, useful work, a home, free speech, a free press, and voting rights. Scenes of reading, worship, mechanical work, and voting accompany their reflections, while the family’s gratitude shifts attention away from luxuries and toward shared well-being and political freedom. The closing prayer expresses hope that the unity within the Johnson household will someday extend to people and nations throughout the world.

ia.creator: Centron Corporation
ia.subject: Patriotism;Holidays: Thanksgiving;Families: 1950s
ia.description: An American family unable to afford a Thanksgiving turkey reviews the things for which they feel thankful. This patriotic film is unusual in that it does not link freedom and happiness with the pursuit of wealth. Produced with nonprofessional actors in Lawrence, Kansas. Written by Margaret Carlile (Trudy) Travis.

forest-in-a-museum-story-of-the-beaver-n.title: Forest in a museum: Story of the Beaver National Forest

DVD Copied by Thomas Gideon.

logic-by-machine-part-ii-a22d2554.synopsis: *Logic By Machine (Part II)* examines how computers derive necessary conclusions from human-supplied premises, data, and operating rules, rapidly performing logical, arithmetic, and control tasks. Through discussion with Professor Nagel and Dr. Hamming, the film considers whether machines can create original ideas, contrasting their speed and accuracy in routine work with the continuing importance of human judgment and problem-solving.

ia.description: 0577 PA8524 Logic By Machine (Computer and the Mind of Man)

american-harvest-part-ii-22cefcd3.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
american-harvest-part-ii-22cefcd3.synopsis: This 1955 Chevrolet-sponsored institutional film portrays automobile manufacturing as central to the U.S. economy, featuring footage of raw-material extraction and processing, factory production, changing landscapes, and mid-century consumerism. Narrated by John Forsythe, it revises a 1951 version.

ia.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
ia.subject: Manufacturing;Automobiles: Economic effects;Sustainability: 1950s
ia.description: This institutional film was designed to promote Chevrolet's corporate citizenship rather than any specific model of automobile. While it forcefully demonstrates how central automobile manufacturing is to the American economy, it even more strikingly shows the effects of the automobile upon our landscape. Bombastic narration is accompanied by excellent images of automobile manufacturing, the extraction and processing of raw materials from the earth, and mid-1950s consumerism. Cinematography: Gordon Avil, Pierre Mols and Robert Tavernier. Music: Samuel Benavie. Narrator: John Forsythe. Revised from the original 1951 version.

ia.subject: Belmont Historical Society Presents; Belmont Media Center; Belmont; Massachusetts; 2000; Belmont Community Moving Image Archive
ia.description: Belmontonian Ralph Burns was born in 1902 and died at 101 years of age on 2/2/2003. Town historian Richard Betts interviewed Mr. Burns on 11/3/2000.

no-time-for-ugliness-part-ii-0adb7226.title: No Time for Ugliness (Part II)
no-time-for-ugliness-part-ii-0adb7226.synopsis: This film examines how thoughtful urban planning can replace visual ugliness with attractive, livable communities. It contrasts billboards, neon signs, concrete, and car-dominated spaces with historic preservation, renewed older districts, housing that retains privacy and individuality, and shopping centers separating vehicles from pedestrians. Citizens are urged to survey local conditions and press leaders for long-range improvements.

ia.subject: need keyword
ia.description: Shows that cities' approaches are marred by billboards and neon signs. Intimates that a demanding citizenry can have these unsightly signs removed.

singing-wheels-3f98801a.creator: H.L. Roberts
singing-wheels-3f98801a.synopsis: *Singing Wheels* traces the evolution of transportation from covered wagons, mule teams, and early automobiles to modern trucking. It presents truck driving as demanding, essential work that supports emergency response and complex modern life. The film emphasizes careful operation, routine inspection, and written performance reports covering a vehicle’s steering, brakes, lights, signals, and overall handling.

ia.sponsor: Motor Truck Committee of Automobile Manufacturers Association
ia.creator: H.L. Roberts
ia.subject: need keyword

back-of-the-mike.title: Back of the Mike
back-of-the-mike.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
back-of-the-mike.synopsis: The film takes viewers behind a radio microphone as performers and sound-effects workers create the final episode of a Western adventure. Actors read scripts around suspended microphones, while other workers use mechanical devices, household objects, and pieces of wood to produce the sounds of cars, telephone calls, a storm, chopping trees, fire, and pursuit. Studio scenes alternate with staged outdoor action, connecting the performers’ work to the adventure heard by the radio audience.\n\nIn the story, Pete Belden and his niece Betty are carrying the Flying B payroll when Sam Hicks and his gang rob them and kidnap Pete. Betty escapes, alerts Sheriff Tom, and helps summon a posse, but the gang sets a fire across a gap to block the pursuit. A car carries the rescuers through the danger, and the closing scene leaves Pete safe with Betty before the radio program bids its audience good night.

ia.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
ia.subject: Media: Radio;Perception: Sound
ia.description: Insider's view of the 1930s radio studio showing the production of dramatic sound effects.

harvest-of-the-years-da0103dc.synopsis: *Harvest of the Years* presents Ford’s integrated automobile manufacturing system, from research and improved production methods to assembly-line construction of cars and engines. It demonstrates studio and location filming, historical reenactments, animation, color, time-lapse, slow-motion, microscopic, telescopic, and X-ray photography, emphasizing that each technique should serve classroom learning.

Furnaces then melt the concentrate into copper matte and slag, emphasizing copper’s essential role in modern electrical appliances and technology.

diesel-story-1c687b86.synopsis: This 1952 film traces the development of the diesel engine from 19th-century steam, gas, gasoline, and hot-bulb engines through Rudolf Diesel’s compression-ignition design. It explains four- and two-stroke cycles, fuel-injection advances, and the diesel engine’s adoption in ships, trains, trucks, tractors, power plants, and other machinery.

ia.subject: need keyword
ia.description: Traces the development of the diesel from the Otto 'SILENT' gas engine of 1877, through Rudolph Diesel's engine, to the machines that now drive ships, trains, tractors, trucks and cars.

choosing-for-happiness.title: Choosing for Happiness
choosing-for-happiness.creator: Affiliated Film Producers
choosing-for-happiness.synopsis: College student Mary reunites with her friend Eve on campus and listens as Eve describes why several romances have failed. Dramatized scenes show Alex craving admiration, Arthur caring more about mathematics than romance, and Steve preferring quiet work in his boat-building shop to Eve’s social life. Eve likes something about each man but wants to change the rest of his personality, while Mary believes that lasting relationships require accepting the whole person.\n\nEve is especially angry with John because he refuses to break a promise to return a borrowed car on time. Mary tells Eve that she was asking John to obey her rather than prove his affection, then advises her to change herself instead of trying to remake others. After considering her own similarities with Steve, Mary concludes that attraction alone does not ensure compatibility. She plans to understand which parts of herself cannot change and to remain friends with a man for a long time before choosing him as a husband.

ia.creator: Affiliated Film Producers
ia.subject: Marriage;Social guidance;Gender roles
ia.description: Premarital advice for young women.

long-distance-09e45519.title: Long Distance
long-distance-09e45519.creator: Audio Productions
long-distance-09e45519.synopsis: This 1941 film surveys America’s long-distance communications network, explaining how telephone wires, radio links, repeaters, switchboards, and teletype systems carry voices, music, news, weather reports, and government messages. It connects telecommunications technology with U.S. expansion and emphasizes the engineers, operators, and maintenance workers who keep the nation connected.

ia.creator: Audio Productions
ia.subject: telephones; communication; Bell System; Manifest Destiny; United States expansion
ia.description: The film "Long Distance" explores the significance of long-distance communication in America, highlighting the intricate network of wires and technologies that connect people across vast distances. It emphasizes the evolution of communication from isolation to unity, showcasing the contributions of engineers, builders, and pioneers in creating a transcontinental network. The narrative intertwines the historical journey of America with the advancements in communication, illustrating how voices, music, and written messages traverse the country and beyond, facilitating connections and sharing vital information. Keywords long distance, communication, network, technology, America, history, unity, pioneers, wires, transcontinental, voice, music, written messages, telecommunications

california-is-climate-ab16dfd5.synopsis: This 1958 promotional film presents the Metropolitan Oakland Area, especially Alameda County, as an attractive place to live and conduct business. ia.description: Promotional film for the eastern San Francisco Bay Area (Alameda and part of Contra Costa counties) emphasizing its excellent weather, advanced infrastructure, and cultural and economic advantages. The film discusses the impact of climate on life in the Metropolitan Oakland Area (MOA), highlighting its mild, even temperatures as a key factor in residents' well-being and productivity. It explains how the local climate minimizes weather extremes, benefiting both individuals and industries by reducing heating and cooling costs. The film emphasizes the area's outdoor recreational opportunities, the growth of the population and industries, and the strategic advantages for businesses due to favorable weather conditions. It also touches on governmental support for industrial development in the region. wake-turbulence-avoidance-146dc680.title: Wake Turbulence Avoidance
wake-turbulence-avoidance-146dc680.creator: Federal Aviation Administration
wake-turbulence-avoidance-146dc680.synopsis: This Federal Aviation Administration briefing explains the physical dynamics and hazards of aircraft-generated wake turbulence through reenactments and animation. It follows pilots and air traffic controllers as they manage approaches, visual separation, runway operations, and missed approaches, emphasizing aircraft size, flight paths, wind, traffic density, and maintaining appropriate spacing or altitude to reduce risk.

connecticut-df4a8491.title: Connecticut
connecticut-df4a8491.creator: Dudley Pictures Corporation
connecticut-df4a8491.synopsis: This educational film presents Connecticut through its Revolutionary and abolitionist history, manufacturing centers, agriculture, cultural life, and recreation. It highlights textiles, hardware, rifles, clocks, and toys; New Haven as an industrial and cultural center; dairy farms and shade-grown tobacco in the Connecticut River Valley; and beaches and boating on Long Island Sound.

working-science-tracking-the-microbes-of.title: Working Science: Tracking the Microbes of Life
working-science-tracking-the-microbes-of.creator: Yvonne Stapp; Belmont Media Center

working-science-tracking-the-microbes-of.synopsis: This 2015 film visits MIT’s Roger Summons Lab, a lead participant in NASA’s Mars Science Laboratory project. It shows geobiologists and astrobiologists selecting and chemically analyzing Earth rock and soil samples for potential biomolecules, then applying those methods to data from the Curiosity rover’s investigation of Martian soil.

ia.creator: Yvonne Stapp; Belmont Media Center
ia.subject: Science For The Public: Working Science; Belmont Media Center; Belmont; Massachusetts; 2015; Belmont Community Moving Image Archive
ia.description: As one of the lead participating labs in NASA's Mars Science Laboratory project, the Roger Summons Lab at MIT analyzes potential bio-molecules in ancient Earth sediments and rocks, and applies that expertise to the search for bio-molecules or their precursors on Mars. the Mars Curiosity Rover investigates soil samples on our favorite planet. In this video, we see how geobiologists/astrobiologists select and chemically analyze rock and soil samples on Earth, and how they also analyze data received from the Mars Curiosity Rover.

weather-spotter-in-action-dramatization-.title: Weather Spotter In Action (Dramatization)
weather-spotter-in-action-dramatization-.creator: Calvin Company
weather-spotter-in-action-dramatization-.synopsis: This 1950 dramatization follows a weather spotter monitoring threatening clouds and weighing the likelihood of a tornado. While others urge him to take a break, he maintains watch over the storm’s southwest approach. When a funnel touches down near a pumping station, he urgently phones the weather bureau to report its location and northeastward movement.

junkyard-guards-caedc91f.creator: Mine Safety and Health Administration
junkyard-guards-caedc91f.synopsis: This 2005 Mine Safety and Health Administration training film follows two teams of mining mechanics and fabricators competing to build effective machine guards from scrap materials found at mine sites. Available in English and Spanish, it demonstrates low-cost guarding solutions and offers fabrication tips and safety best practices.

ia.creator: Mine Safety and Health Administration
ia.subject: msha.gov
ia.description: Mine Safety and Health Administration Junkyard Guards *Videographer Award of Excellence Winner* DVD513-S - 2005 ( English | Spanish ) This unique training product presents a contest between two teams of mining industry mechanics and fabricators whose challenge is to construct effective machine guarding from scrap metal and other old left-over parts from the mine site. This non-interactive DVD demonstrates that cost-effective and reliable machine guards can be fabricated with materials commonly found in the junkyards at most mine sites. Best practices and fabrication tips are presented as well.

a-continent-is-bridged-reel-3-of-4-83da4.title: A CONTINENT IS BRIDGED (Reel 3 of 4)
a-continent-is-bridged-reel-3-of-4-83da4.creator: National Archives and Records Administration
a-continent-is-bridged-reel-3-of-4-83da4.synopsis: Reel 3 of this 1940 Bell Telephone Laboratories film traces advances in long-distance telephony, explaining transposition, loading coils, phantom circuits, repeaters, signal loss, distortion, and noise. Through dramatized historical scenes and technical demonstrations, it shows how engineers extended telephone service across the United States and highlights the value of preserving telephone history.

ia.creator: National Archives and Records Administration
ia.subject: archives.gov;public.resource.org
ia.description: National Archives and Records Administration - ARC Identifier 89093 / Local Identifier BTL-BTL-192 - A CONTINENT IS BRIDGED (Reel 3 of 4) - Bell Telephone Laboratories, Inc. On telephone developments, 1876-1940. Reel 1 shows items in the American Telephone Historical Library and the Historical Museum in New York City and explains their historical significance. Dramatizes John Carty's belief, in 1880, that lines from Baltimore to Chicago will some day exist. Reel 2 dramatizes the signing of the certificate of incorporation of the A.T.T. in 1884 and the stage of improvement in 1892. Diagrams the principle of transposition. Reel 3 explains the use of loading and repeating coils and dramatizes conditions in 1911. Reel 4 reenacts the raising of the last pole for the first trans- continental line at Wendover, Utah, in 1915. Shows scenes of telephone employees at work and encourages historical research. DVD copied by IASL Master Scanner Timothy Vollmer.

belmont-historical-society-presents-the-.title: Belmont Historical Society Presents: The Golden Age of Boston Television
belmont-historical-society-presents-the-.creator: Jeremy Meserve
belmont-historical-society-presents-the-.collection: Belmont Community Moving Image Archive (Internet Archive collection)

The program considers the careers of prominent station personalities, the evolution of news and magazine shows, election coverage and international reporting, and the advertising, financial news, and competitive broadcast culture that shaped Boston television.

ia.description: Former TV critic, journalist, and author Terry Ann Knopf talks about the early days of Boston television. There are some 200 local TV markets in the country, but only one — Boston — was the site of a “Golden Age” of local programming

ia.subject: Media: Television;Electronics

safety-through-seat-belts-45058219.title: Safety Through Seat Belts
safety-through-seat-belts-45058219.synopsis: This educational film examines automobile collisions and the resulting toll of injury and death, emphasizing the forces passengers endure in crashes. Through demonstrations involving road and vehicle movement, it explains how seat belts restrain occupants, reduce injury, and improve survival chances. A family’s travel plans frame the film’s practical argument for consistent seat-belt use.

sleep-for-health.title: Sleep for Health
sleep-for-health.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films
sleep-for-health.synopsis: Using a family’s new baby as a starting point, the film explains that repeated daily actions become habits and urges children to establish a regular bedtime. David and Martha follow quiet evening routines that include washing, hanging up their clothes, wearing loose nightclothes, and preparing comfortable beds with fresh air. As David sleeps, the film describes changes in breathing, body temperature, heartbeat, and muscle activity. A comic dream sequence accompanies the explanation that dreams and turning in bed are normal parts of sleep.\n\nDavid wakes naturally, has time for breakfast, and remains alert through school and recreation. George, by contrast, stays up late listening to threatening gangster dialogue, struggles to fall asleep, and has difficulty getting out of bed. His lack of sleep leaves him forgetful in class, low in energy during games, and irritable with other people. The closing message tells children that a consistent bedtime makes sleep and waking easier and helps them enjoy their day.

ia.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films
ia.subject: Health and hygiene;Dreams;Sleep
ia.description: Told from the viewpoint of a child, this film emphasizes that children should train themselves in good sleeping habits. In typical "Goofus and Gallant" style, it shows the advantages a well-rested kid has over his poor-sleeping classmate. Dreams are presented as a normal part of sleeping, and there is a funny dream sequence.

appellate-case-opening-480ce36f.title: Appellate Case Opening
appellate-case-opening-480ce36f.creator: Federal Judicial Center
appellate-case-opening-480ce36f.synopsis: This 2000 Federal Judicial Center program examines administrative challenges in opening appellate cases and effective court practices involving case screening, communication, docket quality control, briefing schedules, transferred cases, successive applications, and pro se matters.

ia.creator: Federal Judicial Center
ia.description: Federal Judicial Center ava20961vnb1 -- 4045-V/00 (2000) Appellate Case Opening October 5, 2000. This program examines administrative challenges facing appellate courts when cases are opened and presents effective practices courts have adopted to meet these challenges. Discussion focuses on four areas: case screening (the role of staff, case managers, and staff attorneys in case-captioning; case types; consolidating or "companioning" cases; jurisdictional issues); communication (developing concise, detailed letters to attorneys; informing district courts, attorneys, and the public of changes in federal and local rules); quality control (modifications to the docket brought about by public access technology); and other logistics (second or successive applications; the briefing schedule; transferred cases; pro se issues).

a-traveler-meets-air-traffic-control-26c.title: A TRAVELER MEETS AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL
a-traveler-meets-air-traffic-control-26c.creator: National Archives and Records Administration
a-traveler-meets-air-traffic-control-26c.synopsis: This 1963 Federal Aviation Agency film follows a passenger and an FAA specialist aboard a flight from Chicago to Los Angeles, explaining how control towers, radar facilities, flight service stations, navigation aids, and regional control centers coordinate air traffic. dolores-project-archaeology-ebeec4b0.creator: National Archives and Records Administration
dolores-project-archaeology-ebeec4b0.synopsis: This 1979 film documents archaeology associated with the Dolores Project. reflections-mining-history-c0ef709e.creator: Mine Safety and Health Administration
reflections-mining-history-c0ef709e.synopsis: “Reflections” Mining History traces the evolution of U.S. coal mining from poorly supervised, labor-intensive work to mechanized operations governed by comprehensive health and safety laws. energy-the-american-experience-17aedca9.synopsis: This film traces America’s changing reliance on wood, coal, oil, and gas, warns that once-abundant fuels are being consumed rapidly, and examines resource planning alongside scientific and industrial efforts to develop new energy sources.

Students learn that exercise, rest, nutritious food, and supportive shoes can help them develop better posture; demonstrations also show comfortable standing and sitting positions that keep the body aligned. finding-his-voice-an-animated-cartoon-sy.title: Finding his voice : an animated cartoon synchronized to voice & sound
finding-his-voice-an-animated-cartoon-sy.creator: Western Electric Company, Inc.
finding-his-voice-an-animated-cartoon-sy.synopsis: In this animated cartoon, a professor teaches two characters called Talkie and Mutey how synchronized sound motion pictures work. Studio microphones turn speech into an electrical current, and vacuum tubes amplify that current about ten million times. A light valve then varies a beam of light to photograph the sound as a track on film moving at the same speed as the picture film.\n\nAfter development, the separate sound and picture negatives are printed together on a single strip for projection. A lamp scans the soundtrack, a photoelectric cell converts the changing light back into electrical vibrations, and an amplifier sends the signal to loudspeakers behind a perforated theater screen. This arrangement keeps sound in step with the picture and makes voices seem to come from the people on screen; after Mutey gains a voice, the two characters end by singing together.

conquering-roads.title: Conquering Roads
conquering-roads.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
conquering-roads.synopsis: A covered wagon on a paved boulevard and automobiles struggling over rough roads introduce the mismatch between modern vehicles and outdated highways. Cars travel through ruts, blind crossings, congested streets, and railroad crossings as the film tells drivers to slow down, avoid reckless speed, and adjust their driving to road conditions. Wide lanes, banked curves, improved lighting, divided parkways, and widened pavement are shown as ways to reduce hazards and delays.\n\nAerial and ground views explain how traffic circles, cloverleaf interchanges, bridges, underpasses, and separated road levels keep cars and trucks moving without crossing one another’s paths. Examples include approaches to the George Washington Bridge, the Triborough Bridge, and the Pulaski Skyway, along with highway construction in New Jersey and Louisiana. The closing message urges public support for road building and connects improved highways with safer travel, easier access, greater traffic capacity, and savings in time.

machine-master-or-slave-37525f07.title: Machine : Master or Slave?
machine-master-or-slave-37525f07.synopsis: This 1941 film examines how labor-saving machinery affects employment and the economy as defense production expands. Through factory workers and managers confronting automation, layoffs, rising inventories, and failed sales campaigns, it questions how technological progress can be balanced with job security and consumer purchasing power.

ia.description: The film explores the impact of labor-saving machinery on employment and the economy. As factories ramp up production for defense needs, workers face potential layoffs due to automation. The narrative follows a group of factory workers and managers grappling with rising inventories and the challenge of selling increased output at higher prices. Despite aggressive marketing efforts, the lack of consumer purchasing power leads to a failure in sales campaigns. The film ultimately raises questions about balancing technological advancement with job security and the need for economic prosperity to enable consumer spending. delft.synopsis: Made in 1923, the film surveys Delft from high viewpoints and at street level. Rooftops and church towers spread across the skyline, including the Nieuwe Kerk and Oude Kerk, while a man looks down from the Watertoren and the camera examines stone towers and spires.\n\nCanals, bridges, tree-lined streets, and rows of narrow buildings define the city center. Pedestrians and cyclists travel through the streets, a horse-drawn vehicle passes near a bridge, and children gather beneath a brick archway. At a busy outdoor market, vendors work under awnings as townspeople face the camera, followed by close views of a large, richly decorated building.

apollo-13-splashdown-and-recovery.title: Apollo 13 Splashdown and Recovery
apollo-13-splashdown-and-recovery.creator: NASA
apollo-13-splashdown-and-recovery.synopsis: Apollo 13 returns through Earth’s atmosphere while Mission Control tracks the expected end of the communications blackout and the deployment of drogue and main parachutes. Television images show the command module descending beneath its parachutes, and cheers follow confirmation of splashdown near the recovery ship Iwo Jima. The film explains that the crew had traveled around the Moon with help from the lunar module Aquarius after an explosion left the service propulsion system unusable.\n\nHelicopters and swimmers secure the command module with a sea anchor, flotation collar, and raft before opening its hatch. The three astronauts climb into the raft and are lifted one at a time in a rescue net to a Navy helicopter. Closing footage shows men in flight suits walking on the recovery ship and meeting officers, crew members, photographers, and other waiting personnel.

dating-do-s-and-don-ts.creator: Coronet Instructional Films
dating-do-s-and-don-ts.synopsis: When an injured friend sends Woody a ticket for two to a carnival, Woody faces the problem of arranging his first date. He decides that Ann’s friendly manner matters more than looks alone and receives his mother’s permission to ask her. Contrasting versions of the telephone call show that a clear, polite invitation should name the event and time while allowing the other person to consult her parents. Ann accepts Woody’s invitation.\n\nAs Woody and Ann prepare, their families discuss grooming, punctuality, agreed return times, reasonable costs, and saving flowers for especially formal occasions. The couple attends the carnival, where booths, refreshments, costumes, and other young couples are visible. At the end of the evening, several awkward farewells are compared with a courteous goodbye in which both say they had fun and Woody offers to call Ann the next week.

nederlandsche-heide-maatschappij-en-haar.synopsis: This silent section of a promotional film about the Nederlandsche Heidemaatschappij links rural improvement with changes in farming and community life. Cattle graze and are milked by hand, while other scenes cover milk transport and processing, pig and poultry keeping, and farm work performed with both hand tools and machinery. rca-16mm-sound-projector-the.synopsis: White-gloved hands demonstrate how to prepare and thread an RCA 16 mm sound projector, unfolding the reel arms, fastening drive belts, and guiding film through the sprockets, gate, sound drum, rollers, and take-up reel. Close views of the mechanism accompany explanations of how the claw, pressure pads, sprocket shoe, damper roller, and even-tension take-up are intended to reduce wear and prevent breakage. Access panels and movable assemblies show how the projection and exciter lamps can be replaced or cleaned, while the film describes sealed bearings and a brushless induction motor as features that reduce maintenance. Closing product views emphasize fast threading, quiet operation, film protection, a 15-watt amplifier, a bright picture, durability, and ease of use.

dordrecht.synopsis: This 1926 silent film surveys Dordrecht as an industrial city shaped by its waterways. Workers gather at long benches inside a large factory, while closer views show a man operating heavy equipment. Along the waterfront, warehouses, barges, cargo vessels, and tall cranes fill the busy harbor.\n\nFrench-and-German intertitles describe Dordrecht as an important port for transferring raw materials and show coal being unloaded with modern cranes. Another intertitle identifies the Moerdijk Bridge, says that it has 14 arches, and introduces views of its railway tracks and steel trusses. The closing river scenes feature small sailing vessels moving across broad, open water.

gabby-fire-cheese.creator: Jack Ward / Dave Fleischer / Max Fleischer / Paramount Pictures
gabby-fire-cheese.collection: Wikimedia Commons / original source recorded on file page
gabby-fire-cheese.synopsis: This 1941 animated film follows Gabby as he visits a fire station and boasts that he was once known as “Fire-eatin’ Gabby.” When the firefighters rush away, Gabby chases their engine and joins them at a burning house. He orders the crew around but becomes tangled in the equipment and repeatedly interferes with their work.\n\nFirefighters struggle with hoses and ladders while mischievous flames move between windows to escape the streams of water. Gabby grabs a hose and takes part in the increasingly chaotic effort until the fire is finally extinguished. In the closing gag, the firefighters offer Gabby a “token of gratitude” that drenches him, prompting him to complain that he will catch pneumonia.

behind-the-bright-lights.title: Behind the Bright Lights
behind-the-bright-lights.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
behind-the-bright-lights.synopsis: After opening with nighttime views and a love song, the film examines a giant Chevrolet electric sign in downtown Chicago. Workers climb across its steel framework and bulb-covered letters, using ropes and suspended chairs to inspect the display and replace burned-out globes. The film describes the sign as 23 stories high and explains that one moving section, called a motograph, contains more than 8,000 lights.\n\nInside the control room, an electrical engineer monitors machinery that operates the sign’s clock, circular light patterns, and animated messages. Demonstrations show how each bulb connects to a contact brush and how holes punched in a moving paper roll allow selected brushes to touch a copper plate, switching groups of bulbs on and creating the appearance of motion. The closing scenes return to workers high on the illuminated sign and jokingly suggest that they are safer than the pedestrians navigating traffic below.

ia.subject: Advertising: Outdoor;Electricity;Chicago
ia.description: How Chevrolet's giant electric sign in downtown Chicago works.

beginning-to-date.title: Beginning to Date
beginning-to-date.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica Films, Inc.
beginning-to-date.synopsis: Students at Lincoln School prepare for a teen-club party at the community house, where some expect to arrive with dates. George has never asked a girl out, but a coach compares dating with taking a first dive and encourages him to try. George awkwardly but successfully invites Mildred, while alternate versions of Bill’s telephone call show how to identify oneself, explain the invitation clearly, and end the conversation politely.\n\nBefore the party, examples cover grooming, honest compliments, introductions to parents, and choosing conversation topics that interest both people. At the event, the teenagers dance, watch entertainment, and learn not to abandon a partner or remain too long in separate groups of boys and girls. George plans transportation so Mildred can meet her deadline, escorts her to the door, and waits until she is safely inside. The closing message says that courage, advance planning, and consideration for other people make dating more enjoyable.

how-you-see-it.title: How You See It
how-you-see-it.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
how-you-see-it.synopsis: Crowds entering a movie theater introduce an explanation of how separate still photographs appear to move on a screen. Diagrams of the eye and examples involving raindrops, passing scenery, and fireworks describe “persistence of vision,” in which an image seems to remain briefly after its source disappears. Footage of workers handling heavy equipment demonstrates how small changes between successive photographs create apparent motion, while high-speed photography produces slow motion when projected at a normal rate.\n\nThe film then uses diagrams, loose film, and an operating projector to explain how reels, sprockets, an aperture, lenses, a lamp, and a shutter work together. The shutter blocks the light while the film advances, allowing viewers to see each frame only while it is stationary and making the sequence appear continuous. A closing scene of people balanced atop a moving car emphasizes the film’s message that motion pictures can reveal fast action in ways the unaided eye cannot.

ia.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization

ia.description: How persistence of vision makes motion pictures possible.

accidents-don-t-just-happen.title: Accidents Don't Just Happen
accidents-don-t-just-happen.creator: Prelinger Archives
accidents-don-t-just-happen.synopsis: Through hospital scenes and stylized animation, a physician explains that injuries called accidents often have identifiable physical, emotional, or physiological causes. He recalls Fred Taylor, who panics over his sick daughter, falls down a staircase, and breaks his leg, then describes workshop injuries associated with poor eyesight or anger. Further examples connect accident risk with impaired hearing, disease, aging, medication, alcohol, overeating, and emotional distress.\n\nThe physician calls for systematic research into accident prevention while also examining hazards in his own life. He acknowledges unsafe driving, the absence of seat belts, overloaded household wiring, poorly secured medicines, and the decision to let Jimmy use the car despite missing driver training and driving too fast. The film ends with a repeated hospital call for Dr. Marvin to report to surgery, immediately after the concern about Jimmy and the car.

act-your-age.creator: Coronet Instructional Films
act-your-age.synopsis: After Jim scratches a school desk with a pencil bearing his name, an adult at the school has him repair the damage and keeps the pencil until Jim believes he can use it responsibly. Their conversation connects Jim’s conduct to teenagers who lose their tempers, cheat, cry over small problems, show off, or react badly to jokes and disagreements. The film calls these behaviors “infantile reactions” and explains that different parts of a personality may mature at different rates.\n\nJim creates a “How Old Am I?” worksheet that asks how maturely he behaves when he faces disagreement, ridicule, confusion, lack of attention, or disappointment. He compares his own ratings with assessments from his parents and best friend, then plans to control his temper and check his progress over time. After Jim decides that he is ready to reclaim his pencil, the closing question invites viewers to rate their own behavior in the same way.

walk-thru-roof-bolting-machine-trainer-s.creator: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health
walk-thru-roof-bolting-machine-trainer-s.synopsis: Part five of a 2004 NIOSH training series designed to help mine safety trainers teach new operators the knowledge and skills needed to use walk-through roof bolting machines and reduce machinery-related injuries in underground coal mines.

ia.creator: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health
ia.subject: cdc.gov
ia.description: Department of Health and Human Services Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health Walk-Thru Roof Bolting Machine Trainer’s Guide (Part 5) NIOSH 2004-100d - 2004 ( Part 1 | Part 2 | Part 3 | Part 4 | Part 5 | Part 6 | Doc ) Given the expected high turnover of the mining workforce, it is very likely that incoming workers will have much less experience than those leaving the workforce. Unfortunately, inexperienced miners have been shown to incur the highest rate of injuries. The piece of machinery most associated with these injuries is the roof bolting machine, which accounts for 56% of machinery-related injuries in underground coal mining. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) has released a new report entitled “Roof Bolting Machine Operators Skills Training for a Walk-Thru Roof Bolter: Trainer’s Guide” (IC 9489). It is designed to help safety trainers develop structured training for new operators of walk-thru bolting machines. This resource will help trainees learn, understand, and apply knowledge and skills. Included in the trainer’s guide are the following tools: a six-part DVD video series, a skills check survey, talking points, and a complete job training analysis. Also included is an exercise to help trainees learn more about their mine’s roof control plan, as well as a list of supplemental training and reading materials. On-site trainers can modify this guide to fit their particular mine conditions, machines and equipment, and work procedures. This video discusses practical measures for identifying risk factors for violence at work, and taking strategic action to keep employees safe. It is based on extensive NIOSH research, supplemented with information from other authoritative sources.

These scenes record both Amsterdam’s prominent architecture and everyday street life in its older neighborhoods.

The film explains that newborn kittens have closed eyes, then shows their eyes open at two weeks and their change from their mother’s milk to cow’s milk at five weeks. As the kittens grow, they play with yarn, wrestle, learn to wash themselves, follow their mother, and climb an apple tree.\n\nFarmyard encounters teach the kittens to protect themselves: they bristle at a dog, one swats the dog’s nose, and all retreat up the tree. When they are considered old enough to “work,” the farmer’s wife takes two kittens to the village, where a shoemaker and a postmaster expect them to catch mice. The third kitten remains on the farm and is described at the end as the luckiest of the three.

gabby-two-for-the-zoo.synopsis: In this animated comedy, Gabby finds a shipping crate addressed to the Royal Zoo in Lilliput and labeled for a rare “rubberneck Kangal.” After another man insists that no such animal exists, a small, long-snouted creature emerges. Gabby boasts that he can handle any animal and volunteers to deliver the Kangal to the zoo.\n\nGabby’s confidence collapses as the Kangal stretches into a towering animal, resists the leash, and repeatedly changes shape. His attempts to control the creature by making it hold its breath and drink water cause further trouble, including swelling its body to an enormous size. As the exhibit ends, the student hosts thank their guests, who respond graciously. The closing message defines everyday courtesy as the simple practice of being friendly, thinking of other people, and showing respect.

on-the-air.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
on-the-air.synopsis: On the Air opens in a radio studio, where Rubinoff plays violin with an orchestra while control-room staff monitor the broadcast. The film explains that home listeners do not hear the studio sounds directly; microphones convert sound waves into changing electrical currents, which are amplified and sent by wire to a transmitting station.\n\nAt the transmitter, an oscillator produces a carrier wave, modulation combines that carrier with the audio signal, and large tubes amplify the resulting radio wave before an antenna sends it outward. Diagrams and views of broadcasting equipment show how a receiver tunes to one station, separates the audio signal from the carrier, amplifies the current, and uses a loudspeaker diaphragm to reproduce the studio sound. The program closes by inviting listeners to hear Rubinoff and his violin again the following week.

mental-health-keeping-mentally-fit.synopsis: At a high school graduation, a local doctor explains that mental health, like physical health, depends partly on habits that people can learn. Four dramatized stories show Tommy discussing fears that his family no longer wants him, Bruce learning not to demand perfection from himself in tennis, Otto receiving encouragement to join a school camera club and make friends, and Nancy suffering needless worry after postponing her studying.\n\nThe film summarizes four rules: express emotions naturally and with consideration for others, respect your own abilities without expecting perfection, respect and participate with other people, and address problems promptly and honestly. It also recommends discussing troubles with a trusted parent, doctor, teacher, adviser, or clergyman, and describes an engaging hobby as a source of relaxation and accomplishment. The closing message describes these rules as only an introduction to mental health but says they can support happier and more useful lives.

nieuwe-stormramp-in-den-achterhoek.title: Nieuwe stormramp in den Achterhoek

nieuwe-stormramp-in-den-achterhoek.collection: Netherlands Institute for Sound & Vision — Open Images
nieuwe-stormramp-in-den-achterhoek.synopsis: This 1927 silent film records the aftermath of a whirlwind that struck Neede in the Achterhoek. Opening intertitles also name Beltrum and Lichtenvoorde as badly affected and appeal to Dutch viewers for help. Streets and yards are buried under bricks, timber, roofing, and fallen trees, while homes, workshops, and other buildings stand roofless or partly collapsed. Residents and workers cross the wreckage, inspect damaged structures, and climb among broken roof frames.\n\nA locomotive surrounded by debris precedes an intertitle reporting that a 12-year-old girl was thrown under a train and killed. Inside torn-open homes, furniture and household goods remain among fallen masonry; another intertitle describes salvaged belongings as what a brother could still save. Wide views of shattered houses, bare rafters, leaning poles, and extensive rubble convey the storm’s impact on everyday life.

indisch-allerlei.synopsis: Made in 1920 from footage shot by Willy Mullens in the Dutch East Indies, this silent film surveys urban centers, markets, waterways, farmland, and volcanic terrain. Scenes documented as Buitenzorg, Sumatra, Batavia, Fort de Kock, and Bali show crowded markets, harbor traffic, fishing, and women washing in a river. Broad views take in a steep river gorge, terraced fields, tropical vegetation, and smoking sulfur springs; a Dutch intertitle explains that yellow sulfur surrounds the vents and sulfurous gases rise from the ground.\n\nRailway tracks and bridges wind through hills and cultivated areas, linking the landscapes with signs of industry and transportation. A musician plays an instrument in a gamelan ensemble, while other scenes concentrate on groups of Balinese people gathered outdoors and on individual faces and clothing. Together, these images record work, travel, music, community life, and varied environments in the colonial-era Dutch East Indies.

the-house-i-live-in.title: The House I Live In
the-house-i-live-in.creator: Creator listed on Library of Congress item record
the-house-i-live-in.collection: Library of Congress — explicit public-domain National Film Registry set
the-house-i-live-in.synopsis: A male singer finishes a romantic song in a recording studio and steps outside during a break, where he finds a group of boys preparing to attack another boy because of his religion. He challenges their prejudice by asking whether religious differences would matter if blood donated by the targeted boy’s father had saved another boy’s wounded father. The singer tells them that Americans come from many backgrounds, speak in different ways, and worship in different churches, but remain equal members of the country.\n\nTo emphasize cooperation, he recounts a wartime story about a Presbyterian pilot and a Jewish bombardier serving together against a Japanese battleship. He then sings “The House I Live In,” describing America through homes, streets, workplaces, schools, freedom of speech, and people of all races and religions. The boys listen quietly before the singer returns to work and they walk away.

Aerial views show the Vehicle Assembly Building, surrounding roads, parking areas, and broad crawlerways.\n\nAt the launch area, a Saturn V stands upright beside red and gray service structures identified in the source title as Pad 39A. what-is-money.title: What Is Money?
what-is-money.creator: Coronet Instructional Films
what-is-money.synopsis: A five-dollar bill passes among several people after Tom Havens uses it to buy paint. The same bill pays for electrical work and gasoline, helps cash a check, buys bookends, becomes part of a clerk’s radio payment, and returns to Tom as his wages before he deposits it in a savings account. These transactions show money serving as a medium of exchange for goods and services, a standard for comparing prices and setting future payments, and a way to store value.\n\nScenes of barter and objects once used as money explain why a widely accepted currency is more practical in a specialized economy. The film describes desirable money as valuable, recognizable, portable, divisible, and durable, then traces a progression from traded objects to metal coins and government-issued paper bills. Checks are identified as substitutes for money, while confidence in the issuing government is said to support acceptance of currency. The closing summary connects money with business, trade, travel, and exchange between nations.

ia.creator: Coronet Instructional Films
ia.subject: Economics
ia.description: Following the journey of a five-dollar bill through many transactions, the film shows how money functions as a standard of value and future payment, a storehouse of value and a convenient medium of exchange.

Rubble covers large areas, while broken walls, exposed building interiors, twisted structural remains, and clouds of smoke show the scale of the damage. People walk through the ruins and gather near damaged streets and surviving buildings.\n\nLater scenes focus on crowded transportation areas, where pedestrians, horse-drawn wagons, streetcars, and people carrying baggage fill the streets. A large crowd gathers beneath a covered entrance before the closing section shows more people moving with their belongings. An intertitle ends the film with a joke that San Franciscans have wrongly claimed this crowd marked the beginning of Oakland.

over-the-waves.title: Over the Waves
over-the-waves.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
over-the-waves.synopsis: Roller-coaster scenes introduce the discomfort caused by sudden rises and drops, then a car traveling on a paved road shows that even ordinary roads contain waves and bumps. The film explains that a car’s suspension must keep the passenger compartment level while the wheels follow these uneven surfaces.\n\nWorking models use wheels, platforms, springs, shock absorbers, and tracing pens to compare how different suspension arrangements respond to bumps at various speeds. These demonstrations show how soft, balanced springs reduce jolting, while shock absorbers control compression, stretching, and continued bouncing. Views of full-size components connect the models to a Chevrolet suspension system in which parallel arms keep the front wheels aligned and the springs cushion bumps. In the final test, a car carries a smoke-fed tracing device intended to show that the body remains comparatively level as the wheels move over a rough road.

Bobby keeps unnecessary objects off his desk, walks and sharpens a pencil quietly, whispers when he must speak, and retrieves materials without disturbing others; reading and project groups move chairs carefully, arrive prepared, listen when someone speaks, and remain near their work areas. The closing question asks viewers what they can do to make their own classrooms quiet places for work.

A woman and close-up views of the telephone demonstrate lifting the receiver, waiting for the steady dial tone, and turning the dial for each part of a number.\n\nIntertitles distinguish the steady dial tone from the intermittent ringing signal and tell callers to hang up and try again later when a call cannot be completed. After several unsuccessful attempts, callers are instructed to dial the operator for help. The film also warns against releasing the dial before it reaches the finger stop or moving the switch hook while dialing.

something-for-nothing.title: Something for Nothing
something-for-nothing.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
something-for-nothing.synopsis: Cartoonist Rube Goldberg draws and explains absurd inventions, including a chain-reaction door opener and an automatic hat tipper that he identifies as an 1896 patented device. Using another elaborate drawing, he introduces the long-standing dream of perpetual motion: a machine that could run and perform useful work without an outside energy source. The film explains that engines cannot produce power without consuming fuel.\n\nLaboratory scenes, outdoor demonstrations, and an engine model show how gasoline produces power when mixed with air, ignited, and compressed inside a cylinder. The film describes changes to pistons and combustion chambers that improve mixing and compression while limiting engine knock, allowing automobiles to obtain more power from their fuel. Goldberg closes by boasting that he has achieved perpetual motion, but his triumphant speech ends with the comic call, “Oscar!”

ia.creator: Handy (Jam) Organization
ia.subject: Animation: Rube Goldberg;Automobiles: Engineering
ia.description: Cartoonist Rube Goldberg creates a little animation to explain how fuel is converted to power in the modern automobile engine.

video-apollo-11-pre-launch-and-launch.title: Video - Apollo 11 Pre-Launch and Launch
video-apollo-11-pre-launch-and-launch.creator: NASA
video-apollo-11-pre-launch-and-launch.synopsis: NASA’s 1969 film shows crowds and interviewers outside the launch complex, flight controllers working at rows of consoles, and the Apollo 11 Saturn V on its pad. Countdown reports say that all systems remain ready for a planned 9:32 a.m. liftoff, while Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin prepare inside the spacecraft. The film explains checks of the fuel, maneuvering thrusters, escape tower, range-safety system, and other equipment intended to protect the crew.\n\nMission Control in Houston prepares to take responsibility for the flight once the rocket clears the tower. Views of the Saturn V venting on the pad alternate with spectators and control-room activity as the countdown approaches zero. At ignition, a dense exhaust cloud expands around the launch site and fills the closing view.

vertrek-dok-tandjong-priok-naar-nederlan.synopsis: This 1923 film shows the 8,000-ton Tandjong Priok dry dock leaving Rotterdam for the Dutch East Indies. Four tugboats carefully maneuver the enormous structure along the river and beneath the steel Maas bridges. The words “Burgerhout Rotterdam Builders” identify its builder.\n\nSmoke pours from the tugboats as they pull and guide the dock through the industrial waterfront. Workers and onlookers gather on vessels, bridges, and the dock itself, while people in small boats watch from the water. A man calls through a large megaphone as the operation continues, emphasizing the coordination required to move the structure through the confined passage.

trip-down-market-street-before-the-fire-.title: [Trip Down Market Street Before the Fire, A]
trip-down-market-street-before-the-fire-.creator: Miles Brothers
trip-down-market-street-before-the-fire-.synopsis: Made by the Miles Brothers in 1906, the film follows a forward-moving view from a cable car traveling along Market Street in San Francisco. Streetcars, horse-drawn wagons, early automobiles, and pedestrians share the broad roadway, often crossing the tracks directly in front of the camera. Multi-story commercial buildings and crowded sidewalks line the route, while a large clock-towered building grows steadily nearer.\n\nRecorded before the 1906 earthquake and fire, the footage documents the movement, congestion, and varied transportation of a major city street shortly before much of downtown San Francisco was destroyed.

ia.creator: Miles Brothers
ia.subject: San Francisco: Scenics: Historical;Transportation: Cable cars;Landscapes: Cultural
ia.description: PLEASE NOTE: A much higher-quality DV version (2.3 GB) now available at http://www.archive.org/details/TripDownMarketStreetrBeforeTheFire Pictures San Francisco's main thoroughfare as seen from the front window of a moving Market Street cable car, before the downtown area was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake and fire. This unusual record has been called the first "structural film" because it follows exactly the externally imposed structure of the car ride. Here is a post from the SFGate blog that explains some of the history of this film and how film scholar David Kiehn discovered that it was in fact produced in 1906 (just before the quake and fire), not 1905: http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/blogs/stew/detail?entry_id=62237

lens-hollands-dorp-in-frankrijk.synopsis: Made in 1921, this silent film records Lens in northern France after the destruction of the First World War. Roofless buildings, broken brick walls, rubble, and empty window openings show the damaged town. A plaque dated 1919–1921 states that “La Cité Hollandaise” was built for people affected by the war by the Kingdom of the Netherlands with the cooperation of the French government.\n\nWide views reveal the new settlement as rows of similar wooden houses set among roads and garden plots. Dutch emigrants and people of Dutch ancestry lived in the community. A young child stands outside one house, two women meet across a table indoors, and final panoramas emphasize the settlement’s size and uniform design.

ia.description: Charlie Chaplin's 57th Film released November 13 1916. Behind the Screen, a short film written and directed by Charlie Chaplin also starring Eric Campbell and Edna Purviance. In the film which takes place in a movie studio, Chaplin plays a stagehand named David while Campbell ("Goliath") plays his supervisor. Much of the film is slapstick comedy but other issues are also brought up such as a stagehand strike as well as a plotline in which Purviance, unable to become an actress, dresses as a man and becomes a stagehand. The film is silent. The film is noted for having one of the first Hollywood gay jokes in it. After Chaplin learns that Purviance is really a woman, he kisses her while on the set. pathe-news-christmas-with-their-camerame.synopsis: This 1950 Warner Pathé News film opens with a conductor leading a large choir in a grand interior. Newsreel camera operators and crews then offer Christmas greetings from locations across North and South America, Europe, and Asia. Many stand beside motion-picture cameras, with city landmarks or wintry landscapes behind them.\n\nSpeakers identify locations including Hollywood, Paris, Chicago, Washington, Mexico, Seattle, Finland, Tokyo, Berlin, Frankfurt, and New York. Several deliver their greetings in French, Spanish, Portuguese, Finnish, Japanese, or German before the film provides an English translation, while a Washington group includes a costumed Santa Claus. The choir closes with “O Come, All Ye Faithful,” followed by a “Merry Christmas” title.

ia.description: Newsreel cameramen from around the world wish the audience Merry Christmas.

ia.subject: archives.gov;public.resource.org
ia.description: National Archives and Records Administration Space Ship Takeoff, a Technical Fantasy Department of Defense. Department of the Air Force. (09/26/1947 - ) WELTRAUM SCHIFFI STARTET EINE TECHNISCHE FANTASIE (SPACE SHIP TAKEOFF, A TECHNICAL FANTASY). ARC Identifier 67908 / Local Identifier 342-USAF-28533. Summary: A German film depicting, through the use of special effects and animation, the launch of a space ship and its trip around the moon and return. Brief scenes are included of early German rocket power experiments. Selected footage in Reel 1: 410'-432' Early German launch of a small rocket from a trough-type launcher. 436' MS's & CU's of igniters being wired to rockets on the Opel RAK-2 rocket-propelled car. 447' MS to MLS of German rocket pioneer, Max Valier, sitting in his Valier RAK-6 liquid rocket-propelled car. 451' MS of Fritz Von Opel sitting in his Opel RAK-2 rocket-propelled car. 456' MCU of igniters being wired to rockets of Opel RAK-2 rocket-propelled car. 460' LS's of Fritz Von Opel driving his Opel RAK-2 car at Avus Track, Berlin, Germany, 23 May 1928. 472' LS of the Sander-Opel RAK-3 rocket-propelled car run on railroad tracks, 23 June 1928. 475' LS's & MS's of preparations and flight of the Opel-Sander RAK-1 rocket-powered glider, September 1928. 502' LS's firing of a small liquid-powered rocket. 521' MS fueling a rocket-propelled car with liquid oxygen. 531' LS camera pans right with the run of an early model German rocket-propelled car along runway of an airport. 536' CU of Max Valier sitting in the Valier RAK-6 car. 545'-549' MLS ignition of the rockets of the Sander-Opel RAK-3 car mounted on railroad tracks. Good (Basic: Dupe neg) Made possible by a donation from Sabine Kirstein.

what-to-do-on-a-date.title: What to Do on a Date
what-to-do-on-a-date.creator: Coronet Instructional Films
what-to-do-on-a-date.synopsis: Nick Baxter wants to ask Kay on a first date but worries about where they would go and assumes that girls expect expensive entertainment. After Kay has already seen the movie he suggests, Nick invites her to help prepare a scavenger sale at the community center as part of a double date. Nick and Kay work with friends, prepare refreshments, and discover that they enjoy spending time together.\n\nPossible dates shown or discussed include bicycle trips, cookouts, baseball games, swimming meets, miniature golf, bowling, square dances, and concerts. Nick learns to choose an affordable, manageable activity that both people enjoy and to ask his date about her interests instead of making assumptions. After Nick and Kay agree to attend a cookout together, the film closes by advising viewers to look for varied activities, consider the other person, and plan for both people to have a good time.

ia.creator: Coronet Instructional Films
ia.subject: Social guidance;Dating;Teenagers
ia.description: A high school senior learns how and where to ask a girl for a date, where to take her for a good time, and how to avoid spending too much money or being bored by commercialized amusements. Director: Ted Peshak. Cameraman: Dale Sharkey. Writers: George Tychsen, Bradford. Editor: Dick Kirschner. Narrator: George Stone.
